Here we spatially resolve this SO outflow into three components: a collimated jet aligned with the SiO jet, the wide-angle disk outflow, and an evacuated cavity in between created by a large jet-driven bowshock.
The inner part of the wide-angle outflow coincides with the base of the shells and is thus perturbed by the bow shocks.
Its outer part is unperturbed by the bow shocks, providing the best opportunity to check the previously proposed MHD disk wind interpretation (cite: Tabone2017; Tabone2020).
The disk wind is thus dense enough to remove the disk angular momentum, if its SO abundance is close to that in the disk.
